cues.en: All right.
In the previous lecture we have mentioned that there are various types of trees.
Now here in this section we are going to learn about Binary Tree.
Now what is a binary tree?
In previous lecture when we create a basic tree structure, we saw that we have unlimited children for
one node.
So as you can see in the first node we have four children.
Then in this node which is a nine we don't have any children, but for N2 we have two children.
And it continues like this.
Now in case of binary tree, each node has at most two children, often referred as the left and right
children.
It means that any node in the binary tree cannot have more than two children.
So in this case, if we delete these two children from N1, it's going to become binary tree because
in case of binary tree, for one node, we can only have maximum number of two children.
So we cannot have more than two children.
So in this case you can see that for N1 we have two children, for N2 we have two children, and for
N3 we have one child and 4 in 5.
For example, we don't have any child.
So this is going to be the binary tree.
Now the second property of binary tree is that it's a family of data structure.
It means that there are many other tree data structures.
Our type of the binary tree, for example binary search tree is a type of binary tree, heap tree,
AVL tree and and red black tree are all binary tree types.
So to be able to implement these types, we need to learn about binary tree.
Now you might be interested that why we need binary tree.
We need it because all these trees are types of binary tree.
So to be able to implement them, as I mentioned we need binary tree.
And there are more specific problems that can be solved using specific techniques of the binary tree.
Huffman coding problems.
Heap priority problems.
Expression parsing problems can be solved efficiently using binary trees.
So without binary tree this problems become extremely difficult.
So these are the reasons for learning binary tree.
